question.text: A function <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>f</mi><mo>:</mo><mo> </mo><mi>Z</mi><mo>→</mo><mi>Z</mi></math> is defined as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>f</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mi>n</mi></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mfenced close="" open="{"><mrow><mtable columnalign="left" columnspacing="1.4ex"><mtr><mtd><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mtd><mtd><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>odd</mi><mo> </mo><mi>integer</mi></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mfrac><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mtd><mtd><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>even</mi><mo> </mo><mi>integer</mi></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>.</mo></mrow></mfenced></math> If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>k</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>odd</mi><mo> </mo><mi>integer</mi></math> and <math><mi>f</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>k</mi></mrow></mfenced></mrow></mfenced></mrow></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mn>33</mn><mo>,</mo></math> then the sum of the digits of <math><mi>k</mi></math> is

solution.text:
∵ k∈odd integer

fk=k+1 which is even

∴ffk=k+12

If k+12 is odd ⇒33=k+12+1⇒k=63 not possible (because k+12 is even)

If k+12 is even ⇒33=k+122⇒33=k+14⇒k=131

Sum of digits =5
